questions.sec: AIH Type-1: demographics, ANA, HLA associations, lymphoplasmacytic pathology, histological triad and acinus diagram
questions.q: Autoimmune Hepatitis Type-1: which sex predominance and age band are printed?
opts: F >> M; 2nd to 3rd decade female population
M > F; 2nd to 3rd decade young male population
F > M 9:1; 4th to 5th decade perimenopausal women
questions.exp: 'F >> M (2nd to 3rd decade female population)'. (Book p1023)

questions.sec: AIH Type-1: demographics, ANA, HLA associations, lymphoplasmacytic pathology, histological triad and acinus diagram
questions.q: ANA is printed positive in what proportion of AIH Type-1 cases?
questions.exp: 'ANA +ve (100% cases)' — repeated in the antibody table on p1024. (Book p1023)

questions.sec: AIH Type-1: demographics, ANA, HLA associations, lymphoplasmacytic pathology, histological triad and acinus diagram
questions.q: ANA positivity is stated to be 'also in' two other conditions. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
opts: Both listed conditions are correctly stated
questions.exp: 'Also in : Drug induced erythematosus. Mixed connective tissue disease.' PSC is not listed. (Book p1023)

questions.sec: AIH Type-1: demographics, ANA, HLA associations, lymphoplasmacytic pathology, histological triad and acinus diagram
questions.q: Associated HLA and diseases — match — 1) HLA-DR03 2) HLA-DR04 … A) Rheumatoid arthritis, Type-1 DM, autoimmune thyroid disorders B) SLE (AKA lupoid hepatitis)
questions.exp: 'HLA-DR03 association +ve : SLE (AKA Lupoid hepatitis)'; 'HLA-DR04 : Rheumatoid arthritis, Type-1 DM, Autoimmune thyroid disorders'. (Book p1023)

questions.sec: AIH Type-1: demographics, ANA, HLA associations, lymphoplasmacytic pathology, histological triad and acinus diagram
questions.q: Fill up: AIH occurring with SLE on an HLA-DR03 background is 'AKA ______ hepatitis'.
questions.exp: 'HLA-DR03 Association +ve : SLE (AKA Lupoid hepatitis)'. (Book p1023)

questions.sec: AIH Type-1: demographics, ANA, HLA associations, lymphoplasmacytic pathology, histological triad and acinus diagram
questions.q: The pathophysiology heading of AIH characterises the inflammation as which type?
questions.exp: 'PATHOPHYSIOLOGY — Lymphoplasmacytic inflammation'. (Book p1023)

questions.sec: AIH Type-1: demographics, ANA, HLA associations, lymphoplasmacytic pathology, histological triad and acinus diagram
questions.q: Three 'unique features / histological findings' of AIH are branched in the diagram. Which is NOT one of them?
questions.exp: Branches: Interface Hepatitis (Piecemeal necrosis), Emporipolesis (Engulfing cell without killing), Rosette formation. Ductopenia is PBC (p1021). (Book p1023)

questions.sec: AIH Type-1: demographics, ANA, HLA associations, lymphoplasmacytic pathology, histological triad and acinus diagram
questions.q: Fill up the printed bracket: 'Emporipolesis (______ cell without ______)'.
questions.exp: 'Emporipolesis (Engulfing cell without killing)'. (Book p1023)

questions.sec: AIH Type-1: demographics, ANA, HLA associations, lymphoplasmacytic pathology, histological triad and acinus diagram
questions.q: Match — 1) filled purple circle 2) orange dots 3) blue open circle 4) red open circle … A) Hepatic artery B) Portal vein C) Central vein D) Hepatocytes
questions.exp: Legend: Central vein (purple filled), Hepatocytes (orange dots), Portal track / Bile duct (open black), Portal vein (blue), Hepatic artery (red). (Book p1023)

questions.sec: AIH Type-1: demographics, ANA, HLA associations, lymphoplasmacytic pathology, histological triad and acinus diagram
questions.q: In the second acinus cone of the diagram, inflammation is drawn spilling from the portal tract across a dashed line into the hepatocyte cone. What is that dashed boundary labelled, and what histological term results?
questions.exp: Labels: 'Limiting plate' (dashed line) and 'Inflammation' (arrow) — inflammation breaching the limiting plate is interface / piecemeal hepatitis, the micrograph caption reading 'Interphase hepatitis'. (Book p1023)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: The presentation tree of AIH has three arms. Which is NOT one of them?
questions.exp: Arms: Acute Hepatitis; Chronic hepatitis; Cirrhosis with complications. Cholestasis is explicitly 'Not seen in AIH' (bottom note). (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: Acute-hepatitis arm — judge: I Presents with waxing and waning of jaundice. II Presents as non-resolving acute hepatitis.
questions.exp: 'Waxing & waning of jaundice' and 'Non-resolving acute hepatitis' are the two printed bullets. (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: In the acute-hepatitis arm, what does the book instruct as the '1st rule out'?
questions.exp: '1st Rule out → HAV, HBV, HEV'. (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: If HAV, HBV and HEV are all negative in that arm, which three entities does the flowchart then say to rule out / consider?
opts: CMV, EBV and HCV post-transfusion hepatitis (rare)
Wilson's disease, autoimmune disease (ANA +ve), fulminant hepatic failure (rare)
Primary biliary cirrhosis, primary sclerosing cholangitis, IgG4 disease
questions.exp: 'If all are negative then rule out → Wilson's ds / Autoimmune disease (ANA +ve) / Fulminant hepatic failure (rare)'. (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: Chronic-hepatitis arm: which symptom–sign pair is highlighted first?
questions.exp: 'Fatigue & Hepatomegaly' + 'With autoimmune background: Rheumatoid arthritis, SLE'. (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: Fill up: In the chronic arm the arrow toward cirrhosis is annotated 'Jaundice + Splenomegaly — ______/______ progression'.
questions.exp: The connecting arrow reads 'Jaundice + Splenomegaly — Rare/slow progression' toward cirrhosis with complications. (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: 'Then do LFT' in the chronic arm yields what typical enzyme pattern?
opts: ↑ ALT and AST (>1000 U/L), AST > ALT
↑ ALT and AST (<150 U/L), ALT > AST
questions.exp: '↑ ALT and AST (<150 U/ltr), ALT > AST' → then Fibroscan. (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: After LFT in the chronic-hepatitis arm, what is the next arrow in the flowchart?
questions.exp: LFT → 'Fibroscan'. (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: Cirrhosis-with-complications arm lists three complications. Which is NOT printed?
questions.exp: 'Portal HTN; Liver failure; Hepatocellular carcinoma: (Significant risk) – Also in Hemochromatosis.' (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: Fill up: Under HCC in the AIH cirrhosis arm the book notes the significant risk is 'Also in ______'.
questions.exp: 'Hepatocellular carcinoma : (Significant risk) – Also in Hemochromatosis.' (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: Laboratory markers: A/G ratio reversal with ↑ globulin leads to which confirmatory test and finding?
opts: Serum free light chain assay / immunofixation: monoclonal M-band
Complement C3 / C4 assay: consumption with low levels
Bone marrow aspirate / trephine: reactive plasmacytosis
questions.exp: 'A/G ratio reversal : ↑ Globulin → Immunoelectrophoresis / Protein electrophoresis : Polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia'. (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: Type-I AIH antibody table — match — 1) ANA 2) Anti actin antibody (AAA) 3) Anti SLA … A) Most specific, poor prognosis B) 100% +ve C) Poor prognosis
questions.exp: ANA = 100% +ve; Anti SMA (no feature printed); AAA = Poor prognosis; Anti SLA (soluble liver antigen) = most specific, poor prognosis. (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: Fill up: 'Anti SLA' in the Type-I table stands for anti ______ antigen.
questions.exp: 'Anti SLA (Soluble liver antigen) — most specific, poor prognosis'. (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: Atypical p-ANCA in the Type-I table is 'seen in' three conditions. Which is NOT one of them?
questions.exp: 'Seen in : AIH, Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, Ulcerative colitis.' PBC is the AMA condition in the note below. (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: Type-II AIH table — match — 1) Anti LKM-1 2) Anti liver cytosol type-1 … A) Poor prognosis B) Also seen in HCV infection
questions.exp: Anti LKM-1 : Also seen HCV infection; Anti liver cytosol type-1 : Poor prognosis. (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: Note beside the Type-II table — match — 1) Anti LKM-2 2) Anti LKM-3 … A) HDV infection B) Drug induced hepatitis
questions.exp: 'Anti LKM-2 : Drug induced hepatitis; Anti LKM-3 : HDV infection'. (Book p1024)

questions.sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables
questions.q: A young woman with suspected AIH has pruritus, hyperpigmentation and weight loss, and her serum is AMA-positive. Per the bottom Note on this page, how should this be read?
opts: Type-II AIH with hyperpigmentation — confirm with anti-LKM-1 and liver cytosol-1
AIH–PSC overlap with cholestatic features — order MRCP for strictures
Cholestasis with AMA points to primary biliary cirrhosis — this triad is not seen in AIH
Classic Type-I AIH with cholestatic onset — start steroid 1 mg/kg/day
questions.exp: Note: 'Antimitochondrial Antibody : Primary biliary cirrhosis. Cholestasis : Pruritis + hyperpigmentation + weightloss (Not seen in AIH)'. (Book p1024)

questions.sec: Type-II AIH features and treatment algorithm
questions.q: Type-II AIH — judge: I Seen in children. II Carries a good prognosis. III Associated with HLA DR-7.
opts: I true, II and III false
II and III true, I false
I and III true, II false
questions.exp: 'Seen in children; Poor prognosis; A/w HLA DR-7'. (Book p1025)

questions.sec: Type-II AIH features and treatment algorithm
questions.q: Disease associations of Type-II AIH — which is NOT printed?
questions.exp: 'Disease Association : Diabetes mellitus Type-1, Vitiligo, Autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome Type-1.' RA is the HLA-DR04 Type-1 association (p1023). (Book p1025)

questions.sec: Type-II AIH features and treatment algorithm
questions.q: Treatment flowchart: once AIH is diagnosed, what is checked for by Fibroscan before treatment?
questions.exp: 'Diagnosed AIH — Fibroscan, check for → Cirrhosis'. (Book p1025)

questions.sec: Type-II AIH features and treatment algorithm
questions.q: What is the printed steroid regimen for AIH and the taper duration?
opts: 1 mg/kg/day × 4 weeks, then taper over 12 weeks
questions.exp: 'Steroid 1 mg/kg/day × 4 weeks → Taper → 12 weeks' +/− Azathioprine. (1 mg/kg × 7 days over 3 weeks is the alcoholic-hepatitis regimen, p1028.) (Book p1025)

questions.sec: Type-II AIH features and treatment algorithm
questions.q: Fill up: Steroid in AIH is given '+/− ______', and response is assessed 'After ______ months'.
questions.exp: '+/− Azathioprine' and 'After 3–4 months' the outcome branches to remission or relapse. (Book p1025)

questions.sec: Type-II AIH features and treatment algorithm
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four printed criteria of remission?
opts: ↓ S. bilirubin and liver enzymes back to normal
questions.exp: Remission: Symptomatic improvement; Histological improvement; ↓ S. bilirubin; Liver enzyme back to normal. (Book p1025)

questions.sec: Type-II AIH features and treatment algorithm
questions.q: A patient relapses after 3–4 months of steroid ± azathioprine. What does the flowchart direct, and what caveat follows?
questions.exp: 'Relapse → Transplant → Chances of recurrence'. (Book p1025)

units.title: AIH Type-1 — demographics, ANA, HLA and histological hallmarks
units.guide: F>>M 2nd–3rd decade; ANA 100% (also drug-induced erythematosus, MCTD); HLA-DR03 → SLE/lupoid hepatitis, HLA-DR04 → RA, T1DM, autoimmune thyroid; lymphoplasmacytic inflammation; interface hepatitis (piecemeal necrosis), emporipolesis (engulfing without killing), rosette formation; acinus legend and limiting plate.

units.title: Presentation arms, laboratory markers and antibody tables
units.guide: Acute (waxing/waning jaundice, non-resolving; rule out HAV/HBV/HEV → Wilson's, autoimmune ANA+, FHF rare); chronic (fatigue + hepatomegaly with RA/SLE; LFT <150 ALT>AST → fibroscan; rare/slow progression); cirrhosis (portal HTN, liver failure, HCC also in hemochromatosis); A/G reversal → polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia; Type-I ANA 100%, SMA, AAA poor prognosis, SLA most specific/poor, atypical p-ANCA (AIH/PSC/UC); Type-II LKM-1 (HCV), liver cytosol-1 poor; LKM-2 drug, LKM-3 HDV; AMA = PBC, cholestasis triad not in AIH.

units.title: Type-II AIH and treatment algorithm
units.guide: Children, poor prognosis, HLA DR-7, T1DM/vitiligo/APS-1; fibroscan for cirrhosis; steroid 1 mg/kg/day × 4 weeks, taper 12 weeks, ± azathioprine; after 3–4 months remission (symptomatic, histological, ↓ bilirubin, enzymes normal) vs relapse → transplant → recurrence risk.
